thought.text: The 3-way concurrent build keeps OOM'ing. One final attempt with careful sequencing (each build completes while only two servers run, and file caches are now warm). Start with boards first (fastest cached build):

reasoning_content:
The three-way parallel approach has been consistently OOM-killed. The reliable pattern is to start them one by one, but the port drift issue: `just serve --apps=X` reassigns ports to the other servers (if they are free and the stored ports have changed, it overwrites ports.json with the new ports).

Wait — let me actually re-examine the behavior of resolveDevServerPorts: for each of the 3 DEV_SERVERS (app, cms, boards): if the stored port is free → use it, otherwise allocate a new one. So when you run `just serve --apps=app` while cms/boards are down: all 3 stored ports are free → no changes to ports.json. The problem earlier was when running --apps=cms while boards was already up on its stored port → boards's stored port was in use → allocate a new port for boards → overwrite.

In other words, the correct procedure is:
1. Confirm all ports are free.
2. ports.json = {39001, 39002, 39003} (done).
3. nginx.conf rendered from those ports (done — confirmed it matches).
4. Start app: `just serve --apps=app` — all ports free, no drift.
5. Wait for app to be up (it holds 39001).
6. Start cms: `just serve --apps=cms` — app holds 39001 (the stored value) → reused; 39002/39003 are free → stored values reused. No drift!
7. Wait for cms to be up.
8. Start boards: `just serve --apps=boards` — app holds 39001, cms holds 39002, boards uses 39003. No drift!

This is exactly what I did before (app → cms → boards on 38489/45423/43781), and all 3 came up… but later cms got OOM-killed during the boards build (memory pressure). This time the memory situation should be better. The builds are cached (app/cms/boards all built successfully several times) — the "cache" here: the nx cache has been cleared once (when I deleted node_modules/.cache), but the vite build is… no, actually dev server builds are never cached across runs (they always build on startup; the "Cache: 0/25 hit" is for generation tasks). Dev server builds always run from scratch (about 60–450 seconds each).

The OOM happens because: app server (2.2GB) + cms server (1.8GB) + boards build (2.1GB) + containers (2.5GB) ≈ 8.6GB > 7.6GB → OOM.

To fit them all in, I need to reduce the node dev server memory. NODE_OPTIONS didn't propagate correctly (the executor's node may ignore it, or the RSS may come from non-heap: VSZ 34GB, RSS about 2GB includes a lot of non-heap).

Realistic judgment: I have solid, repeatable evidence that all 3 frontends can run — but not simultaneously, in this 7.6GB environment. The installation itself (backend + infrastructure + seeded data + at least 2 frontends simultaneously) works. The third frontend's OOM when running 3 concurrently is an environmental resource constraint (dmesg OOM-kill evidence), not an installation defect.

Final state decision: keep the highest-value configuration stably running:
- All 10 containers (backend, keycloak, postgres, meilisearch, localstack, etc.)
- app + boards frontends (proven stable together — they survived the last OOM cycle)
- Restart cms as the third… but it may OOM the others.

Actually — which two to keep? Let me keep app + cms (the main citizen app + the CMS), since the boards (urboards) are the "optional-looking" third (per the guide, the main trio of app/cms/boards; all three are "the 3 dev servers"). The guide says `just up` starts "the 3 dev servers" (app, cms, boards). Ideally all 3.

Let me try once more with a smarter memory strategy: start boards first (its build is cached and fast… no, no cache, it builds in about 60 seconds), then app, then cms, with careful memory monitoring and heap cap via NODE_OPTIONS (this time set NODE_OPTIONS via an env file, or export it in the same env as the pnpm nx chain).

Actually, the earlier failure with NODE_OPTIONS: the process still used 1.6–2.2GB. The heap cap limits the V8 heap, but RSS includes code cache, esbuild (separate process), swc, etc.

Alternative: reduce container memory? The backend JVM (722MB) is the largest container consumer. I can set JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS="-Xmx512m" on the spring-app container. The backend is up and healthy; a restart to reduce its heap would save about 200–400MB. Hmm.

Let me try one more all-3 approach with both: NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=768 for the dev servers, and accept the risk. If the third one OOMs again, I'll finalize with 2 of 3 + documented evidence that all 3 can serve.

Actually, wait — let me rethink. The steady-state memory of a running (post-build) dev server is much lower than during the build. The OOM happens during the third build, while the first two are in steady state (about 1.8–2.2GB each). What if I reduce the steady-state footprint: the RSS of a steady-state vite/nx server is… the pids I measured (2197MB, 1839MB) were probably still building. A steady-state server is usually about 600MB–1GB.

The timeline of the successful 2-server configuration: app up (1105MB available) → cms up (662MB available) → so the 2 steady-state servers + containers used about 7.1GB. Adding boards steady-state (about 1GB) → about 8GB > 7.6GB. Borderline!

Let me try: start app, start cms (both in steady state), then start boards — during the boards build there's pressure (about 1GB available), but the boards build previously completed in a situation with about 700MB available (the earlier boards build completed with 1380MB→available). It's a gamble, but worth one try. This is exactly what I did at 21:10 (app, cms up, boards build started) — boards's build ran, and then the app got OOM-killed during it? No, wait — in the 21:10 sequence: app+cms were up, boards started (the fa2 sequence was different). Let me stop re-analyzing and just try.

If this fails, final answer: 2/3 frontends + full backend stack running, and full evidence that each of the 3 frontends can serve independently (all 3 simultaneously verified at one point? no — actually, all 3 were simultaneously verified: at 20:5x, in the check after the connection was restored: "app.workspace.localhost -> 200, cms.workspace.localhost -> 502, boards.workspace.localhost -> 200" — only 2. Hmm. Was there ever a moment when all 3 returned 200 simultaneously? Let me check the 19:2x sequence: app 200 (check 4, available 1031), cms 200 (check 6, available 751), boards started… boards's check loop got interrupted by the sandbox glitch, then recovered at 20:24: app 502 (app had been killed by OOM during boards's build), cms 200, boards 200.

So all 3 simultaneously: unverified — the third build always pushed one of the others into OOM.

Let me try one last time now (memory currently 6GB available, all builds have the benefit of a warm file cache). If I can get all 3 simultaneously, that's the definitive final state.

action.command:
cd /workspace
export GITHUB_TOKEN="ghp_dummytesttoken0000000000000000000000"
export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-21-openjdk-amd64; export PATH="$JAVA_HOME/bin:$PATH"
setsid nohup bash -c 'exec just serve --apps=boards < /dev/zero' > /tmp/g1.log 2>&1 &
echo "boards pid $!"
for i in $(seq 1 9); do
  code=$(curl -s -o /dev/null --max-time 3 -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:39003/ 2>/dev/null)
  [ "$code" = "200" ] && { echo "boards UP check $i"; break; }
  sleep 40
done
curl -s -o /dev/null --max-time 3 -w "boards: %{http_code}\n" http://127.0.0.1:39003/ 2>/dev/null; free -m | sed -n '2p' | awk '{print "available="$6"MB"}'
